questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 1 source-linked method
questions.prompt: The curve y=ln x is stretched parallel to the x-axis by scale factor 3. Give the new equation, its domain and its x-intercept. [4 marks]
markPoints: A horizontal stretch by factor 3 replaces x by x/3.
So the new equation is y=ln(x/3).
The argument must be positive, giving x>0.
At the x-intercept ln(x/3)=0, so x=3.
questions.modelAnswer: A horizontal stretch by factor 3 replaces x by x/3. So the new equation is y=ln(x/3). The argument must be positive, giving x>0. At the x-intercept ln(x/3)=0, so x=3.

questions.prompt: For a small angle θ measured in radians, obtain the first non-constant approximation to cos(3θ) and state when it applies. [3 marks]
markPoints: Use cos u≈1−u²/2 when |u| is small in radians.
questions.modelAnswer: Use cos u≈1−u²/2 when |u| is small in radians. Put u=3θ. Therefore cos(3θ)≈1−9θ²/2, valid when |3θ|≪1.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 1 source-linked method
questions.prompt: Use the trapezium rule with two equal strips to estimate ∫₀¹1/(1+x) dx. Give an exact fraction and say whether the estimate is above or below the exact value. [4 marks]
markPoints: The ordinates are f(0)=1, f(1/2)=2/3 and f(1)=1/2.
The exact integral is ln2≈0.6931; 17/24≈0.7083 is an overestimate.
questions.modelAnswer: With two strips h=(1−0)/2=1/2. The ordinates are f(0)=1, f(1/2)=2/3 and f(1)=1/2. Trapezium estimate=(h/2)[f(0)+2f(1/2)+f(1)]=(1/4)(1+4/3+1/2)=17/24. The exact integral is ln2≈0.6931; 17/24≈0.7083 is an overestimate.

questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 1 source-linked method
questions.prompt: Solve log₁₀(x+1)+log₁₀(x−2)=log₁₀18, explaining which algebraic root is invalid. [5 marks]
markPoints: The solutions of the quadratic are 5 and −4, but only x=5 satisfies the logarithm domain.
questions.modelAnswer: The log arguments require x>2. Combine logs to give log₁₀[(x+1)(x−2)]=log₁₀18. Therefore (x+1)(x−2)=18. Expand and factor x²−x−20=(x−5)(x+4)=0. The solutions of the quadratic are 5 and −4, but only x=5 satisfies the logarithm domain.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 1 source-linked method
questions.prompt: Evaluate exactly ∫₀^(π/3) x cos(3x) dx using integration by parts. [5 marks]
markPoints: Take u=x, dv=cos(3x)dx, so du=dx and v=sin(3x)/3.
At π/3 the value is cosπ/9=−1/9; at zero it is 1/9, so the integral is −2/9.
questions.modelAnswer: Take u=x, dv=cos(3x)dx, so du=dx and v=sin(3x)/3. Use ∫u dv=uv−∫v du. Thus ∫x cos(3x)dx=x sin(3x)/3−∫sin(3x)/3 dx. An antiderivative is x sin(3x)/3+cos(3x)/9. At π/3 the value is cosπ/9=−1/9; at zero it is 1/9, so the integral is −2/9.

questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 1 source-linked method
questions.prompt: A sequence satisfies u₁=100 and uₙ₊₁=0.6uₙ+20. Find u₂, u₃ and the limiting value, explaining why the limit is plausible. [5 marks]
markPoints: Since 0<0.6<1, the deviation from 50 shrinks by factor 0.6 each step; terms approach 50.
questions.modelAnswer: u₂=0.6×100+20=80. u₃=0.6×80+20=68. At the limit L=0.6L+20. Therefore 0.4L=20 and L=50. Since 0<0.6<1, the deviation from 50 shrinks by factor 0.6 each step; terms approach 50.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 1 source-linked method
questions.prompt: Express d=9+3cos t−4sin t in the form 9+Rcos(t+α), with R>0 and 0<α<π/2. State the minimum possible value of d. [5 marks]
markPoints: Expand Rcos(t+α)=Rcosα cos t−Rsinα sin t.
Since cos ranges from −1 to 1, the minimum of d=9+5cos(t+α) is 4.
questions.modelAnswer: Expand Rcos(t+α)=Rcosα cos t−Rsinα sin t. Compare coefficients: Rcosα=3 and Rsinα=4. Hence R=√(3²+4²)=5. tanα=4/3, so α=arctan(4/3)≈0.9273 radians. Since cos ranges from −1 to 1, the minimum of d=9+5cos(t+α) is 4.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 1 source-linked method
questions.prompt: For y=4ˣ, use four left-end rectangles over 0≤x≤1 to obtain an exact area estimate. Find the exact integral and say whether the rectangle estimate is high or low. [6 marks]
markPoints: The four rectangles have common width h=1/4.
Because y=4ˣ is increasing, left-end rectangles underestimate the exact area.
questions.modelAnswer: The four rectangles have common width h=1/4. Left-hand heights are 1, √2, 2 and 2√2. Estimated area=(1/4)(1+√2+2+2√2)=3(1+√2)/4. Integrate 4ˣ to obtain 4ˣ/ln4. Exact area=[4ˣ/ln4]₀¹=3/ln4. Because y=4ˣ is increasing, left-end rectangles underestimate the exact area.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 1 source-linked method
questions.prompt: The curve x²+xy+y²=7 passes through (1,2). Differentiate implicitly and find the equation of its tangent at this point. [5 marks]
questions.modelAnswer: Differentiating x² and xy gives 2x+y+x(dy/dx). Differentiating y² gives 2y(dy/dx), so 2x+y+(x+2y)(dy/dx)=0. Rearrange to dy/dx=−(2x+y)/(x+2y). At (1,2), the gradient is −4/5. The tangent is y−2=−(4/5)(x−1).

questions.series: Original Year 13 Pure, June 2023 Paper 1 source-linked method
questions.prompt: Express 1/(9−4x²) in the form A/(3−2x)+B/(3+2x). Find A and B. [4 marks]
questions.modelAnswer: Factor the denominator: 9−4x²=(3−2x)(3+2x). Multiply through to obtain 1=A(3+2x)+B(3−2x). Set x=3/2: 1=6A, so A=1/6. Set x=−3/2: 1=6B, so B=1/6.
